label: A rational power is fixed toward a being it gives only if the giver's end requires that being
paraphrase: OPEN (WN, analyst formulation, unattributed): if y gives x being at w by exercising a rational power and is fixed toward x from w (NECESSITATE_5: gives x being at w and at every accessible world where y exists), then x is required by y's own end (EndRequires y x: y's own good could not be had without x). The structure of ST I q.19 a.3 co. (navigation only): the will is necessarily related to its end and to what the end cannot be had without, not to other things. Rivals: the necessary diffusion of the good (Neoplatonic emanation; Avicenna's First) and the moral necessity of choosing the best (Leibniz; Rowe), on which a perfect will is fixed toward effects its own good does not require.
